data.long_meaning: Bikrant is a Sanskrit name derived from the Sanskrit word 'bikrant', meaning 'conquering', 'victorious', or 'progressive'. This name is often given to a child who is expected to overcome challenges and achieve great things in life. The name Bikrant carries the meaning “Conquering, Victorious” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Bikrant usually hope their child will grow to embody conquering, victorious and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Bikrant total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name Bikrant carries a strong implication of strength, courage, and determination in the Hindu culture. It signifies the valor and spirit of a warrior, reminding the bearer to face challenges head-on and never back down. The name is also associated with the idea of progress and upward mobility, suggesting that the individual will make significant strides in their personal and professional growth throughout their life.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Bikrant inspires the individual to embrace their inner warrior, tapping into their inner strength and courage to overcome adversities and obstacles. The name also serves as a reminder of the importance of continuous self-improvement and spiritual growth, encouraging the individual to strive for excellence in all areas of their life. Ultimately, the name Bikrant embodies the Hindu philosophy of dharma, or living a righteous and virtuous life, encouraging the bearer to live a life of purpose and meaning, as a conqueror of their own destiny.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Bikrant signifies the one who is progressing forward, triumphing over challenges with unyielding spirit and courage, forever advancing on the path of self-realization and growth.

historical_references.reference: Bikrant Chandra was a king of the Sena dynasty in Bengal. He ruled from 1170 to 1206 CE. During his reign, he expanded his territory significantly, defeating various rivals and Islamic invaders. He is particularly known for his military prowess and his patronage of Hindu learning and culture.

Bikranti Deva was a king of the Gahadavala Dynasty in northern India. He ruled from 1240 to 1260 CE. During his reign, he successfully defended against Mongol invasions and expanded his territory through military conquests. He is also remembered for his patronage of art and architecture.
